_comment: HVAC implications per climate hazard. Hazard categories are FEMA National Risk Index types (https://hazards.fema.gov/nri/). Per-hazard HVAC impact and pro-action copy is derived from standard industry post-event practice. All action sentences route to a technician or call-a-pro path per Cool Call Pro editorial policy (CLAUDE.md). Consumed by scripts/add_state_hub_climate_hazards.py and generate_state_hubs.py.

noaa_ncei.label: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

Hurricane.impact: Wind-driven debris bends condenser coil fins and post-storm flooding contaminates compressor electricals.
Hurricane.action: Schedule a technician inspection after any named-storm landfall before restart.

Tornado.impact: Flying debris bends coil fins and fan blades on the outdoor unit.
Tornado.action: A technician assesses damage and determines whether the coil must be replaced.

Severe Thunderstorm.impact: Lightning strikes and grid surges destroy contactors, capacitors, and control boards.
Severe Thunderstorm.action: A qualified electrician should install whole-home surge protection.

Hail.impact: Large hail flattens condenser coil fins and restricts airflow.
Hail.action: A technician assesses damage and determines whether repair or coil replacement is needed.

Ice Storm.impact: Freezing rain coats the outdoor coil and blocks the heat pump defrost cycle.
Ice Storm.action: Call a technician — do not chip ice off the unit.

Extreme Cold.impact: Single-digit temperatures stress gas furnace heat exchangers and drive heavy auxiliary heat strip usage on heat pumps.
Extreme Cold.action: Schedule a pre-winter tune-up before the first hard freeze.

Blizzard.impact: Deep snow drifts bury outdoor units and block furnace intake and exhaust vents.
Blizzard.action: A technician should clear buried equipment and verify venting before restart.

Extreme Heat.impact: Compressor failures rise sharply when outdoor temperatures sustain above 105°F.
Extreme Heat.action: A technician should verify refrigerant charge and capacitor health before heat waves.

Wildfire.impact: Heavy smoke clogs standard filters within days and draws soot into the indoor coil.
Wildfire.action: Replace your filter with a MERV 13 during active smoke events and schedule a technician coil inspection afterward.

Flooding.impact: Floodwater above the electrical panel of the condenser or air handler destroys affected components.
Flooding.action: A technician must inspect any submerged equipment before restart — never power up a flooded unit.

Earthquake.impact: Ground movement can shear refrigerant lines, condensate drains, and gas connections at joints.
Earthquake.action: After any measurable quake, a technician should verify refrigerant and gas-line integrity before operation.

Nor'easter.impact: Heavy wet snow combined with high winds damages outdoor equipment and blocks furnace venting.
Nor'easter.action: A technician should clear the unit and verify venting once the storm passes.

Lake-Effect Snow.impact: Sustained heavy snow buries outdoor heat pumps and restricts intake vents.
Lake-Effect Snow.action: A technician should clear the unit and confirm the defrost cycle is completing.

High Wind.impact: Sustained high winds topple poorly-anchored outdoor units and drive debris into coil fins.
High Wind.action: Inspect with a technician after any extreme wind event before restart.

Winter Storm.impact: Sustained heavy snow and low temperatures strain furnaces and bury outdoor heat pumps.
Winter Storm.action: A technician should inspect outdoor equipment and verify the heat exchanger after prolonged cold events.

Volcanic Activity.impact: Volcanic ash abrades coil fins and overwhelms standard filters.
Volcanic Activity.action: Replace your filter with a MERV 13 during ashfall and schedule a full technician coil cleaning once air quality returns to baseline.

Dust Storm.impact: Wind-driven dust scours coil fins and clogs filters within hours.
Dust Storm.action: Replace filters more often during monsoon season and schedule a pro coil cleaning before cooling season ends.

Tropical Storm.impact: Saturated ground, wind-driven rain, and lightning damage outdoor units even without a hurricane-level wind.
Tropical Storm.action: Schedule a post-storm technician inspection before restart.

Coastal Flooding.impact: Saltwater inundation accelerates electrical corrosion and destroys compressor windings.
Coastal Flooding.action: Assume any saltwater-submerged unit requires replacement — a technician must assess before any restart attempt.
